deck.audience: ML researchers and NLP engineers working on tool-augmented LLMs and RLHF alignment

brief.title: DiaTool-DPO: Enhancing Tool-Augmented LLM Dialogue via Direct Preference Optimization
brief.one_liner: A novel DPO-based method that models TA-LLM interactions as an MDP with 5 dialogue states and 3 query types, automatically constructing preference pairs to improve slot-filling and tool call rejection without human labeling.
brief.goal: Understand how DiaTool-DPO formulates tool-use dialogue as a reinforcement learning problem, how its paired trajectory dataset is constructed, and how it achieves near-GPT-4o conversational performance on smaller open-source models.

slides.title: DiaTool-DPO: Multi-Turn DPO for Tool-Augmented LLMs
slides.objective: Cover slide with paper title and key tagline about improving TA-LLM dialogue flow via direct preference optimization with automatic paired trajectory construction.

slides.title: SFT Alone Fails to Teach Slot-Filling and Tool Rejection
slides.objective: Explain the core problem: TA-LLMs trained only with SFT struggle with incomplete queries (missing arguments) and out-of-scope requests, leading to hallucinated tool calls. Describe the three failure modes — failing to ask follow-up questions, making hallucinated tool invocations, and failing to reject inappropriate tool calls — and motivate the need for preference optimization.

slides.title: Modeling TA-LLM Dialogue as a 5-State Markov Decision Process
slides.objective: Visualize the 5 internal states (Initial, Tool Selected w/o Complete Slots, Tool Selected w/ Complete Slots, Wait for Tool Response, Complete) and their transitions. Reference the state diagram from figure_1.jpg.

slides.title: Three Query Types Define Distinct State Trajectories
slides.objective: Show the three query types and their state trajectories: Type 1 (1→3→4→5, sufficient info), Type 2 (1→(2*N)→3→4→5, incomplete info), Type 3 (1→1, out-of-scope). Use a compact table mapping query type to trajectory and example.

slides.title: Automatic Paired Trajectory Construction Without Human Labels
slides.objective: Present the DiaTool-DPO dataset construction: chosen vs. rejected trajectories for each query type, learning lessons (prevent redundant slot-filling, prevent slot hallucination, tool call reject/accept). Display the dataset composition table with counts and difficulty levels.

slides.title: SFT + DiaTool-DPO Achieves Best Macro Average Across All Models
slides.objective: Show the main results table comparing DiaTool-DPO-only, SFT-only, and SFT + DiaTool-DPO across Prop.-8B, Prop.-3.1B, and LLaMA-3-8B on Call, Completion, Slot, Relevance, Micro Avg, and Macro Avg metrics. Highlight that SFT + DiaTool-DPO consistently achieves the highest Macro Avg.

slides.title: LLaMA-3-8B: +43.5% Slot Accuracy and +10.5% Relevance with DiaTool-DPO
slides.objective: Focus on the LLaMA-3-8B results showing dramatic improvements in Slot (0.639→0.917) and Relevance (0.826→0.913) when adding DiaTool-DPO to SFT. Use a bar chart or before/after comparison to emphasize the gains.

slides.title: Key Takeaways: RL-Based Dialogue Control for Production TA-LLMs
slides.objective: Summarize 4-5 key findings: MDP formulation enables systematic trajectory pairing; automatic dataset construction eliminates human labeling; DPO complements SFT for dialogue control; approach is language-agnostic; opens path to GPT-4o-level conversational tool use on smaller models.
